findings.where: First screen, the section drawing: the amber-hatched third bay of the aqueduct, beside the amber 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: The drawing's third bay is in sodium amber, the colour the palette keeps for the one action. In the first view, a piece of decoration and the button share the action's colour. This weakens the rule that amber means 'act here' and gives the eye two amber targets.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank visitor scanning the first screen for the way to get in touch. Amber is the only warm colour on the sheet, so it reads as the action. When decoration also wears it, the button no longer stands alone as the one thing to do.

findings.where: Motion sketch tile: 'REPLAY THE CUT', compared with the underlined article link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' in the article specimen
findings.fault: 'Replay the cut' is a button that runs something on the page, but it is styled like the article link: underlined bold text. On this sheet the underline means both 'go to another page' and 'do something here'. The button also has no button carrier, such as a fill or an edge.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and later builders, who take the button and link looks from this tile. A visitor who sees an underline expects to be taken somewhere, not to have the drawing replay in place.

findings.where: Title block in the top bar: the 'DRAWING MMM-GA-001' and 'SCALE NTS' cells, next to the nav cells. On desktop they sit in the nav row; on phone they sit in the top row above the nav.
findings.fault: The static drawing-number and scale cells use the same ruled box, spaced capitals and white text as the PROFILE / ARTICLES / BLOG / CONTACT links. This is worst on phone, where they sit right next to the logo link. They look like two more nav items that do nothing.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor reading the top bar as navigation, who taps 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page and gets nothing. It is a small false affordance in the place visitors look to find their way around.
